name: Question 5
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14114695/assets/1b03f2ecd03a89d9484e7d28ab4cb34656b288c3a4554c9a4eeacbe9b61f692c.png)

Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}x\,dA,\,$
where $D$ is the region enclosed between the curves ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=4$ and $y=2-x,$ above the line $y=1,$ as shown in the picture.
worked_solution:
Notice that $D$ is a type II region. Since $x\ge 0,$ we obtain the following equations in terms of $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=4 & \,⟹\,x=\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}} \\ y=2-x & \,⟹\,x=2-y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's determine the limits of integration.

- To determine the $y$-limits, we need to find the $y$-coordinates of the points at which the curves intersect. So, we set the following equation and solve it for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}} & =2-y \\ 4-{y}^{2} & =(2-y)^{2} \\ 4-{y}^{2} & =4-4y+{y}^{2} \\ 2{y}^{2}-4y & =0 \\ y(y-2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, since our region lies above the line $y=1,$ the $y$-limits are 
$1\le y\le 2.$

- To determine the left and right functions, we draw a horizontal arrow from left to right through the region, as usual.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14114695/assets/f8fedf15e26f64fc344bd7db6ffaa659bd7c130f36f4a39389b6108136836104.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 2,\,2-y\le x\le \sqrt{4-{y}^{2}}}.
$$

So, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
{∬}_{D}x\,dA={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{2-y}^{\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}}}\,x\,dx\,dy
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{2-y}^{\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}}}\,x\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{2-y}^{\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}}}x\,dx]dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\,\frac{1}{2}[\,{x}^{2}\,]_{2-y}^{\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}}}\text{ }dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\,\frac{1}{2}(4-{y}^{2}-(2-y)^{2})dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\,(2y-{y}^{2})dy\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}\,(2y-{y}^{2})dy & ={[{y}^{2}-\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =(4-\frac{8}{3})-(1-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
